The Assistant Dean of UNEX Public Programs oversees UC Berkeley Extension's academic division, which includes multiple academic departments and a broad portfolio of self-supporting, college-credit-granting programs. This position provides strategic leadership in academic planning, program development, operational effectiveness, partnership cultivation, financial management, and personnel oversight. The Assistant Dean of UNEX Public Programs works under the direction of the Dean to establish division strategy, drive academic innovation, ensure high-quality program delivery, and strengthen Extension's alignment with campus priorities. The position functions with a high degree of autonomy and serves as a senior representative of Extension in collaborations with campus units and external partners.
Academic Program Administration

Directs and administers independent academic programs with complete responsibility for administrative and programmatic activities, including assisting with the design and development of the academic programs developed; independently oversees Extensions academic division, including multiple academic departments and their full range of college credit-granting programs (Science, Mathematics and Biotechnology, Health Sciences, Arts & Humanities, Business & Management, Engineering & Technology).

Provides overall leadership for Extensions academic division of multiple academic departments responsible for generating $17M in annual gross revenue; Directly supervises Academic Directors, ensuring effective academic governance, professional conduct, and alignment with campus Principles of Community; Oversees divisionwide administrative and programmatic activities, ensuring consistent implementation of work processes, tools, and quality standards.
Academic Planning and Effectiveness

Assesses program effectiveness, and recommends changes to program content, policies, and procedures accordingly; Leads short and long-term academic planning across departments, including program development, renewal, and restructuring; Ensures academic quality through systematic program review, curriculum updates, and alignment with institutional strategy; Collaborates with faculty, Academic Directors, and subject-matter experts to design new courses, certificates, and formats of instruction; Integrates best practices in assessment, student feedback, and academic effectiveness.
Partnerships and Revenue Generation

Identifies and pursues funding opportunities and revenue streams; Develops and leads partnership strategies with campus units, higher education institutions, professional organizations, and industry partners; Represents the division in external collaborations, supporting program innovation, enrollment pipelines, and strategic growth initiatives; Builds advisory relationships to ensure programs reflect industry trends and workforce needs.

Participates in advanced program budgeting and accounting processes to support a self supporting/sustaining financial infrastructure of the program; Oversees budget and financial planning for Public Programs; Ensures financial viability of programs in a fully self-supporting environment; Determines resource allocation across departments and recommends adjustments based on performance, enrollment, and strategic priorities; Collaborates with Extension's Chief Operating Officer and Budget & Financial Services on financial risk assessment and contract feasibility.
Personnel and Resource Management

Manages financial and HR resources; directly supervises professional staff, exercises full supervisory authority, including assigning work, monitoring performance, conducting annual performance evaluations, and managing recruitment, onboarding, and disciplinary actions.

Provides technical guidance and identifies professional development opportunities to ensure team goals are met. Oversees a team of 23-25 staff members and 500+ instructors directly and through subordinate managers; Provides leadership in conflict resolution, grievance handling, and staff support; Builds a positive, collaborative culture and models One Berkeley values.
Interdisciplinary Collaboration

Facilitates the efforts of various departments, managers, and outside constituencies to ensure interdisciplinary collaboration; Leads implementation of standardized administrative processes, academic quality frameworks, and agile work practices across departments; Ensures efficient coordination between academic and administrative units, including Marketing, Recruitment, Finance, IT, Student Services, Inclusion, and Registrar; Drives continuous improvement in workflows, systems, and cross-departmental collaboration.

Represents the division on committees, boards, and strategic planning groups; Participates in professional conferences and public-facing events; Supports strategic projects for the Dean's Office and contributes to institution-wide initiatives.
Excellent leadership abilities to oversee multiple functions or departments through subordinate managers.
Able to manage, lead, and supervise operations and staff in a production, customer-service, and results-driven department.
Strong leadership and political acumen with a commitment to excellence in service.
Able to quickly come up to speed in areas outside personal expertise, ask good questions, and challenge assumptions.
Advanced knowledge of administrative, budgetary, human resources, and financial principles and practices.
Advanced oral and written communication skills.
Advanced ability to think creatively and independently on concepts requiring advanced analytical skills.
Advanced interpersonal skills and ability to work with diverse groups to achieve results.
Advanced ability to work collaboratively with internal and external peers and managers.
Advanced knowledge of concepts, principles, and procedures of building and maintaining effective relations with internal and external, national and international constituencies.
Advanced intercultural communication skills to effectively manage relations with staff, agents, and representatives of institutional or corporate partners.
Excellent ability to establish metrics for department and employee goals that measure the effectiveness of contributions to efficient operations of the department.
Advanced verbal and written communication and interpersonal skills with ability to build beneficial relationships with internal and external departments and professional organizations.
Advanced skills in strategy development, systems planning, and change management.
